r0.why: Constraint on rational solutions, integer coefficients, a0 and an nonzero, alternate names and roots/zeros all in [1],[2].

r1.why: Finds all rational roots [5], finite checkable candidates [6], factoring out (x-r) by long division gives lower-degree polynomial [7].

r2.why: Clearing by q^n [12], factoring p [13], coprime plus Euclid's lemma gives p divides a0 [14], q rearrangement against an [15].

r3.why: Both examples, candidate lists, results and the three-roots remark match [21]-[25].

r4.why: Eight candidates [26], tedious/tricks [29], negatives excluded [30], P(1)=1 [31], 2 ruled out [33], only P(2/3) computed [34], single root 2/3 [28].

r5.why: Three complex solutions [8], cube roots if no rational root [9], quadratic formula after factoring out (x-r) [10].

r6.why: Special case of Gauss's lemma for a single linear factor [3]; integral root theorem when an=1 [4].
